newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - India edges up on selective demand.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - India edges up on selective demand.

text.p: Indian GDRs crept higher in quiet trade on Monday as holidays in many Asian markets dampened activity, traders said.
Selective demand appeared in key stocks to offer support, but they said the market was likely to remain subdued ahead of the Indian budget at the end of the month.
"Clients remain selective buyers but ahead of the budget things do not look good for the market," one trader said.
He said demand had appeared for State Bank of India and Reliance among others, while some selling had appeared for EIH, which lost 31 cents to $21.25.

He said the market could also be hampered in coming weeks by a GDR issue by VSNL. The company said it had finalised an international syndicate for its proposed GDR issue and expected an issue to take place in the first quarter of 1997.
A trader said current premiums to local market prices were likely to ease. "Either the local market must rally or we will go lower," he said.
SBI added 15 cents to $18.37/19.37 and Reliance picked up five cents to $14.50/15.50.
Bombay's benchmark 30-share index ended 36.33 points up at 3,443.55.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index closed 0.11 points or 0.16 percent up at 68.14, with the premium over the local market at 15.36 percent from 15.68 percent on Friday.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended up 0.65 points at 66.61 with a premium of 44.26 percent over the local market.
The Taiwan GDR Index finished down 0.32 points at 100.35, with a premium of 3.79 percent to the local market.
